title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Butter Ovens
summary: Winter comes to Chelm and everyone is freezing, but there is no clay and no lime to build ovens. Reb Shmerel's solution? Ovens made of butter! Everyone brings butter, they build a shiny yellow oven and light a fire... and then, drip, drip, butter does what butter does. But little Gitele knows just what to do with a yellow puddle. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
Winter came to Chelm, and everyone shivered and shook,
the big and the small, the old and the young — just look!
"Brrr! Brrr! How do we get warm?" they all cried.
"Maybe we should build some ovens, cozy inside?"

They went to Reb Shmerel, the wisest, most important of men,
and asked, "How do we not freeze? This cold is too much again!"
He raised one finger and said, "Build ovens — that's the solution!"
And everyone cheered, "Hooray! How wise! What a brilliant conclusion!"

Off they went to build ovens, but oh dear, oh my:
no clay for the bricks, no lime, no stuff anywhere to try!
Yokel searched every basket, every hole and every pail —
no clay, no lime, not even a spoon, to no avail.

Back they went to Reb Shmerel: "No clay, no lime, no sand!"
He thought, and paced slowly, then called out loud and grand:
"There's butter in every house, in bowls and in jars!
Build ovens of butter — and you'll be warm all winter, by the stars!"

Everyone brought butter, in bowls, in baskets and pails,
and Yokel dragged a pile as tall as the sky, without fail.
Butter, butter, soft and yellow —
our oven won't be cold for any fellow!

Reb Kalman stacked the blocks, Reb Zalman spread a layer,
and up stood a shiny yellow oven, like a little sun, bright and fair.
Butter, butter, soft and yellow —
our oven won't be cold for any fellow!

A merchant rode by in a red wagon, wearing a tall hat on his head,
he looked at the yellow oven and raised an eyebrow, and said:
"Chelmites, Chelmites — won't the butter melt away?"
And everyone cried, "Let's ask the wise man!" — and ran off without delay.

Reb Shmerel pondered and pondered, and said, "You're right, you're wise —
it will melt, that's true. But there's no clay — so build warm ovens, that's my advice!"
And the Chelmites nodded, "He's right! What a giant brain!"
And went back to building oven after oven, singing a happy refrain.

They lit fires in the ovens and sat all around, full of cheer,
and a sweet smell rose up, and they all shouted, "Success is here!"
Butter, butter, soft and yellow —
our oven won't be cold for any fellow!

Drip, drip — the first wall melted and turned all soft,
then the second, then the third — and nothing stayed aloft.
Butter, butter, melted and yellow —
now will it be cold? Oh yes, poor fellow!

Gitele brought a challah and cut it, slice after slice,
dipped them in the puddle and gave everyone some, warm and nice.
The Chelmites ate and laughed and hugged their tummies, and suddenly — what a treat!
Even without an oven, they felt warm inside, from head to feet.

A new winter came, the cold came back, and everyone shivered and shook,
the big and the small, the old and the young — just look!
The Chelmites ran for butter in bowls: "We'll build again, like last year!"
And Gitele knitted a scarf and smiled: "I'm ready, my dear."
